Surah al-Jumu'ah (The Congregation)

It is Medinan, and its verses number eleven.

Muslim narrated in his Sahih, from Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) "used to recite in the Friday prayer [the surah] al-Jumu'ah and [the surah] al-Munafiqun."

(p-٥٧٩٧) In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted, saying:

[1–2] ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies God, the King, the Pure, the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ ﴿It is He who sent among the unlettered a messenger from among themselves, reciting to them His verses, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom, although they had been before in manifest error.﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 2]

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies God, the King, the Pure, the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ ﴿It is He who sent among the unlettered﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 2], i.e., the Arabs, ﴿a messenger from among themselves﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 2], i.e., from their own selves, unlettered like them, ﴿reciting to them His verses﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 2], i.e., although he was unlettered like them and no reading or learning had been known from him, ﴿and purifying them﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 2], i.e., from the vile beliefs and morals, ﴿and teaching them the Book and wisdom﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 2], i.e., the Qur'an and the Sunnah, ﴿although they had been before in manifest error﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 2], i.e., in deviation from the truth and departure from the path of guidance. This is an explanation of the intensity of their need for a prophet to guide them.

Ibn Kathir said: God, glorified and exalted, sent him during a period of lull among the messengers and the effacement of the paths, when the need for him had become acute. That is because the Arabs had formerly adhered to the religion of Abraham, peace be upon him, but they altered and changed it, substituting polytheism for monotheism and doubt for certainty, and they innovated things God had not sanctioned. Likewise the People of the Book had altered their scriptures, distorted them, and misinterpreted them. So God sent Muhammad (ﷺ) with a great, complete, comprehensive law for all creation, containing their guidance and the explanation of everything they need regarding their livelihood and their hereafter, calling them to what brings them near to Paradise and the pleasure of God, and forbidding what brings them near to the Fire and the wrath of God, a decisive judge over all doubts, suspicions and uncertainties, in matters of principle and of detail. (p-٥٧٩٨) And God, to whom belong praise and bounty, gathered in him all the excellences of those before him and gave him what He had given no one of the earlier nations, and will not give to anyone of the later ones. So may God's prayers and peace be upon him always until the Day of Judgment. End of quotation.

The reason the mission was singled out among the unlettered (may God's prayers and peace be upon him) is that they were among the most acute of minds, the strongest of hearts, the purest of natural disposition, and the most eloquent in expression. Their innate nature had not been corrupted by the blemishes of the civilized, nor by the artful deceits of those urbane people. For this reason, after Islam, they turned to the people with great knowledge, brilliant wisdom and just governance, by which they led most of the nations and subdued the greatest kingdoms. The singling out of the mission among them—in the sense of its manifestation among them—does not contradict the universality of the message, as He, glorified is He, said:

﴿Say: O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of God to you all﴾ [al-A'raf: 158], and His saying:

﴿that I may warn you thereby and whoever it reaches﴾ [al-An'am: 19], and this is the apparent meaning of His saying:

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[3] ﴿And others among them who have not yet joined them. And He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾

﴿And others among them who have not yet joined them. And He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ is coordinated with "the unlettered" (al-ummiyyin).

That is: He sent him to the unlettered people of his time, and to others among the unlettered who have not yet joined them, but who will join them. These are those who come after the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, from everyone who enters Islam until the Day of Resurrection, as Mujahid and others explained, and as Ibn Jarir (Ibn Jarir al-Tabari) chose.

al-Razi said: The unlettered (al-ummiyyin) here means the Arabs, and "others" means those other than them from the nations. He counted them among them because, when they embrace Islam, they become of them. All Muslims are one community, even if their races differ. Allah the Exalted says:

﴿And the believing men and the believing women are allies of one another.﴾ [al-Tawbah: 71] End of quote.

(p-5799) Alert:

Some of the verifiers said: In the verse there is one of the miracles of prophethood, namely the report of an unseen matter that has occurred, and the glad tidings of the entry of non-Arab nations into Islam, which has indeed taken place. Those nations that embraced Islam have become Arabs, because their lands became lands of the Arabs, their language became the language of the Arabs, and likewise their religion and customs, until they became Arabs in race, religion and language. The term "Arab" came to be applied to all Muslims of every race, because they are one community: ﴿And indeed this, your community, is one community﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 52]. Allah the Mighty has spoken truly.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[4] ﴿That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is the Lord of tremendous bounty.﴾

﴿That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is the Lord of tremendous bounty.﴾ That is, His sending a Messenger to the Unlettered (al-ummiyyin) and to others is a bounty which He has bestowed upon the one He chose and selected for it. He knows best where to place His message. These verses are a refutation of those among the Jews of Madinah who denied his prophethood (ﷺ), out of envy and obstinacy, even though they possessed among the signs of his message what their hearts cannot doubt the truthfulness of. Therefore He reproached them for opposing what their knowledge required, by His saying, glorified is He:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, may He be exalted:

[5] ﴿The likeness of those who were charged with the Torah, then did not carry it, is like the likeness of a donkey carrying books. Evil is the likeness of the people who denied the signs of God. And God does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾

﴿The likeness of those who were charged with the Torah, then did not carry it, is like the likeness of a donkey carrying books﴾ Al-Zamakhshari said: He likened the Jews, in that they are the bearers of the Torah and its reciters and the memorizers of what is in it, and then they do not act upon it nor benefit from its signs. That is because in it is the description of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and the glad tidings of him, yet they did not believe in him. "Like the donkey carrying books" means great books of knowledge; it walks with them and understands nothing of them except what passes by its sides and back of fatigue and toil. And everyone who has knowledge but does not act upon it, this is his likeness, and evil is the likeness! ﴿Evil is the likeness of the people who denied the signs of God﴾, namely the Jews who denied the signs of God, which indicate the truth of the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ). The meaning of ﴿were charged with the Torah﴾ is that they were obligated to know it and to act by it; then ﴿did not carry it﴾ means they did not act by it, so in reality it is as if they had not carried it, due to the absence of action. End of quotation.

The Imam Ibn al-Qayyim said in "I'lam al-Muwaqqi'in": He compared the one whom God, glorified is He, entrusted with His Book, so that he might believe in it, reflect upon it, act by it and call to it, and then he opposed that and did not carry it except upon the back of his heart; his recitation without reflection, without understanding, without following it, without judging by it, and without acting upon its requirements, is like a donkey on whose back is a load of books, which does not know what is in them, and its share of them is only carrying them on its back. So his share of the Book of God is like the share of this donkey from the books on its back. This likeness, although it was struck for the Jews, applies in meaning to whoever has been entrusted with the Qur'an and then abandons acting by it, does not discharge its right, and does not observe it with its proper observance. End of quotation. ﴿And God does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾, that is, those who wronged themselves, so they disbelieved in the signs of their Lord.

Discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[6] ﴿Say: "O you who have become Jews, if you claim that you are allies of Allah to the exclusion of [other] people, then wish for death, if you are truthful."﴾

﴿Say: "O you who have become Jews, if you claim that you are allies of Allah to the exclusion of [other] people, then wish for death, if you are truthful."﴾ The Jews used to say: "We are the sons of Allah and His beloved ones." So it was said to them: "If you are truthful in your claim, and certain of your matter, then wish upon Allah that He cause you to die and swiftly transport you to the Hereafter. For the beloved longs for the meeting of the one he loves and does not flee from it, and desires to rest from the afflictions and griefs of this world, and to arrive at the comfort of the Gardens and their bounties."

The Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on Surah 62, verses 7–8:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[7–8] ﴿But they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent forward. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾ ﴿Say, "Indeed, the death from which you flee will surely meet you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do."﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 8]

﴿But they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent forward﴾, i.e., because of the sins, evil deeds and disbelief [they have committed]. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers﴾, i.e., He will recompense them for their deeds. The parallel of this verse has already been mentioned in al-Baqarah: ﴿Say, "If the final abode with Allah is yours exclusively, to the exclusion of the people, then wish for death, if you should be truthful."﴾ [al-Baqarah: 94]

﴿Say, "Indeed, the death from which you flee"﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 8], i.e., you fear that you would wish for it with your tongues, fearing that it would strike you, so that you would be held accountable for your deeds. ﴿Indeed, it will surely meet you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 8], i.e., of the deeds, good and evil, and He will recompense you for them.

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[9-10] ﴿O you who have believed, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Jumu'ah, hasten to the remembrance of Allah and leave off trade. That is better for you, if you only knew.﴾ ﴿And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land and seek of Allah's bounty, and remember Allah often that you may succeed.﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 10]

﴿O you who have believed, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Jumu'ah﴾ means: when the imam sits on the pulpit [p-5802], because there was no call other than this one during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). "When he sat on the pulpit, Bilal would call the adhan, may Allah be pleased with him." ﴿hasten to the remembrance of Allah﴾ means: to the khutbah and the prayer. ﴿and leave off trade﴾ means: at that time. Abu Malik said: some people used to sit in Baqi' al-Zubayr, buying and selling, when the call to prayer on the day of Jumu'ah was made, so this was revealed. ﴿That is better for you﴾ means: your striving toward it and leaving off trade is better for you than what yields little benefit and only a comparable profit. ﴿if you only knew﴾.

﴿And when the prayer has been concluded﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 10] means: it has been performed and completed. ﴿disperse within the land and seek of Allah's bounty, and remember Allah often that you may succeed﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 10] means: remember His command, His religion and His law constantly, so that it becomes a firm disposition (malakah) for you, whose effects appear in your deeds and character, and thus you will succeed in the happiness of both abodes.

Ibn Jarir said: that is, remember Him by praising Him and thanking Him for what He has bestowed upon you of success in performing His obligations, so that you may succeed, attaining your desires with your Lord and reaching eternity in His gardens.

**The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:**

[11] ﴿And when they see a trade or a diversion, they rush toward it and leave you standing. Say: "What is with Allah is better than diversion and better than trade, and Allah is the best of providers."﴾

﴿When they see a trade﴾ means a caravan (*'ir*) of trade. ﴿Or a diversion﴾ means whatever the soul is diverted by from truth and beneficial seriousness. ﴿They rush toward it﴾ means they hasten toward the trade, fearing that they will be beaten to it. The pronoun for it (*ha*) is used because the trade is the more important object of their intent. ﴿And leave you standing﴾ means standing on the pulpit (*minbar*). ﴿Say: "What is with Allah"﴾ means the reward hoped for from listening to the sermon and being admonished by it. ﴿Is better than diversion and better than trade﴾ means because the reward's benefit is everlasting, unlike what they imagine from those things.

Al-Shihab said: The mention of diversion first is because it is more blameworthy, so it fits to put it first in a context of reproach.

(p-5803) ﴿And Allah is the best of providers﴾ means: so work for the enduring rewards with Him, for they are better than the perishing matters that you have. Entrust the matter of provision to Him through reliance on Him and trust in His bounty, for He is the best of providers.

**Notes:**

**First:** Al-Razi said: The connection of the Friday verse to what precedes it is that those who were Jews flee from death for the enjoyment of this world and its pleasures, and those who believed buy and sell for the enjoyment of this world and its pleasures in the same way. So Allah, exalted is He, alerted them with His words: ﴿Then hasten to the remembrance of Allah﴾ [62:9], meaning: toward what benefits you in the Hereafter, which is attending the Friday prayer, because the world and its enjoyments are perishing, while the Hereafter and what is in it are lasting. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the Hereafter is better and more lasting﴾ [87:17]. Another aspect of the connection was stated by some: Allah refuted the claims of the Jews in three respects. They boasted that they were the friends and beloved of Allah, so He refuted them with His words: ﴿Then wish for death, if you are truthful﴾ [62:6]. They claimed to be the People of the Book while the Arabs had no book, so He likened them to a donkey carrying books. And (they had) the Sabbath, which Muslims did not have a like of, so Allah legislated the Friday prayer for them. End.

Al-Mahayimi said regarding the connection: Allah, exalted is He, made clear that the requirement of faith is gathering for good, especially giving thanks for humanity, lest it turn into donkey-ness or beast-ness. This is in contrast to the gathering of the People of the Book for evil, which led them to donkey-ness and beast-ness.

**Second:** Al-Suyuti said in *al-Iklil*, regarding His words: ﴿When the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, then hasten to the remembrance of Allah and leave off trade﴾ [62:9]: it indicates the legislation of the Friday prayer, the call to it, the hastening toward it, and the prohibition of trade after the call. Those who said that attendance at Friday prayer is only obligatory upon one who hears the call derived evidence from the verse. Those who said that it does not require the permission of the ruler argued that He, exalted is He, made hastening obligatory and did not stipulate anyone's permission. Those who said it is not obligatory upon women argued that they are not included in the address to males. End.

(p-5804) **Third:** In *al-Iklil*, regarding His words: ﴿Then when the prayer has been concluded, disperse in the land﴾ [62:10]: it permits dispersal after the prayer, from which it is derived that the sermon is to be placed before it. End.

Its apparent meaning is that no other prayer is legislated after its performance, except that he (ﷺ) used to perform two voluntary rak'ahs after it in his house. In another narration: four. As for the belief that the obligatory noon prayer must be performed after it when it is multiplied (in one locality), it is sectarian fanaticism without proof. I have said in the introduction to the *Collection of Sermons*, in the fourth benefit, something of this sort:

The need in these lands at these times calls for more than one Friday congregation, since people do not have one mosque that can hold them, and it is not possible for them to have a single Friday prayer at all. However, its departure from the limit where there is no difference between it and the rest of the prayers in many small mosques that were not built for such a purpose has been greatly exaggerated by al-Subki in his *Fatawa*, because it is something that its legislation rejects, and what the practice of the three generations followed, and even its name as "Jumu'ah," for the pattern *fu'lah* in the language is for intensification. In sum, the great congregational mosques to which crowds come on Friday, and for which establishing it there is a clear need for its neighbors, are those for which there is no disagreement regarding their permissibility however many there are, and those after which the noon prayer is not repeated. We have expounded on this in our book *Reforming the Mosques from Innovations and Customs*.

**Fourth:** His words: ﴿And seek of Allah's bounty﴾ [62:10] indicate the non-legitimacy of suspending the day of Friday. It contains an allusion to avoiding imitation of the People of the Book in suspending the days of Saturday and Sunday, and a rebuttal of what has been innovated in it of duties that lead to disengaging from every work. The principle is that whatever the Wise Book has not explicitly stated, nor the Prophetic guidance, from an upright report, is legislation that Allah has not permitted. And since Allah, by His bounty, has lifted from us the burdens and shackles that were upon those before us, how is it that we drag them back upon ourselves through weak causes? O Allah, grant forgiveness.

(p-5805) **Fifth:** Al-Suyuti said in *al-Iklil*, regarding His words: ﴿And when they see a trade or a diversion, they rush toward it and leave you standing﴾: it indicates the legislation of the sermon, standing during it, the requirement of congregation for the prayer, their hearing of the sermon, and the prohibition of dispersing (away from it). End.

In the two *Sahihs*, it is related from Jabir, who said: A caravan once arrived at Madinah while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was delivering the sermon, so the people went out, and only twelve men remained. Then this verse was revealed: ﴿And when they see…﴾ the verse...

Ibn Jarir related from Jabir, who said: When they married, the slave-girls would pass by with drums and flutes, leaving the Prophet (ﷺ) standing on the pulpit and dispersing toward them, so Allah revealed: ﴿And when they see…﴾ the verse...

And from Mujahid: "Diversion" is the drum.
